chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa from Ali ibn Asbat from Isma'il ibn Mansur from some of his companions from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

"When four grandmothers gather, two from the father's side and two from the mother's side, one of the mother's grandmothers is discarded by lot, and the one-sixth share is divided among the three. Likewise, when four grandfathers gather, one of the father's grandfathers is discarded by lot, and the one-sixth share is divided among the three."
ai.seo_question: How is the one-sixth inheritance share distributed among four grandmothers in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* details the specific application of *al-ramy* (casting out) in Shia jurisprudence to resolve conflicts among multiple grandmothers or grandfathers. It establishes that when four grandmothers (two paternal, two maternal) or four grandfathers are present, one is randomly eliminated to ensure the remaining three share the fixed one-sixth (*suds*) portion, reflecting the scholarly principle of avoiding fractional complexity in inheritance distribution.
